items.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: And then I heard Coleman Hawkins, and Prez. Now when I heard Hawk, he didn’t knock me out like Lester Young did.

ctx.x: Were people still playing, were they selling the C melodies back then too?

I don’t know, they probably were because I saw some, but the C melody, the C melody, no that wasn’t — and then again, I really didn’t know either alto or tenor. Like I just wanted a saxophone you see? And then when I went to the theater and saw Lester Young and — no I didn’t see Lester Young but I mean I heard him on the records with Count Basie — well first of all, Jimmy Dorsey was my first inspiration, Jimmy Dorsey. So he played alto, so okay, well that could have been one of the reasons why I liked that. Then…

said no I like that better than the others. Then I heard Coleman Hawkins, and Prez. Now when I heard Hawk, he didn’t knock me out like Lester Young did. But when I got older, I realized that Hawk was playing the changes better than Lester Young. But Lester Young had that beat and that sound, you know [scats]. Oh I like that boy. And then when I heard Charlie Parker and Dizzy, I said that settles that. That’s it. Yep. So that’s how that happened. And then I was drafted in the Air Force. And they said, “Does anyone…

items.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And so I was on that with the -- it was like, Teddy Wilson [phonetic sp.] on piano, George -- Bob Crenshaw [phonetic sp.] bass, Louie Belson [phonetic sp.] drums, Benny Carter [phonetic sp.], Coleman Hawkins [phonetic sp.], Lou Simms [phonetic sp.], Clark Terry [phonetic sp.], Dizzy, and myself.

ctx.x: Just to be there, you know, see all the cats and. And, listen, like we'd be playing and we're on 52nd St., right? So we'd be playing and I'd look up and people that I've admired for years, they'd be coming in. I'd look up and -- and in come Coleman Hawkins [phonetic sp.]. I'd look up, Don Byas come. Lester Young. You know, like. Bam! They just, you know. Damn. You know. So that was really exciting see all those, you know, Ben Webster [phonetic sp.], Billy Eckstein [phonetic sp.], you know. Wow, man! And this club…

Oh, oh, there was something -- let me just go back to the Air Force for one minute 'cause there was one thing I forgot to ask you when we took the break. When you left the Air Force, the Armed Services still, at that point, were not integrated?
